To qualify at the GS-9 grade level, your resume must demonstrate at least one (1) full year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-7 grade level in the federal sector.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the ability, skill, and knowledge to successfully perform the duties of this position and is typically in or related to this line of work. Examples of specialized experience include performing the following types of tasks on a regular basis.

Using statistical analysis, and software to interpret data and identify trends. Reviewing current or new operational procedures, or workflows to determine impact, and recommending processes or procedures for compliance.

Assisting in the budget formulation process by analyzing and summarizing budget related information; responding to questions related to the process and preparing budget packages. Utilizing technology platforms and software to compile reports, produce charts and graphs and monitor projects or program status.

NOTE: All experience statements (i.e., duties, specialized experience, or related applicable assessment) copied from this announcement and pasted into your resume will not be considered as a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. NOTE: Education can be substituted for experience at this grade level.

To substitute education for experience, you must meet one of the following: A. Master's degree or equivalent graduate degree, or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B or J.D, in a related field of study, (e.g., Business Administration or Business Management). B.

A combination of specialized experience and graduate education as described in "A" above. Only graduate education in excess of the amount required for a GS-07 may be used to qualify applicants for the GS-09.

Therefore, only graduate education beyond the first year of graduate study is qualifying for the GS-09 National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Werde Teil von Enpal Pro und gestalte den Aufbau eines schnell wachsenden Scale-ups mit. Wir vertreiben Hardware sowie Enpal-Services an Handwerksbetriebe und treiben gemeinsam die Energiewende voran.
Unser Ziel ist eine Solaranlage auf jedem Dach, ein Speicher in jedem Haus und ein E-Auto in jeder Garage. Enpal macht das möglich mit einer integrierten Gesamtlösung für dezentrale Energie – von Solaranlage und Batteriespeicher über Wallbox, Smart Meter bis zur Wärmepumpe. Herzstück ist unsere KI-gestützte Plattform Enpal.One +, die tausende Systeme intelligent vernetzt und Strombezug sowie -einspeisung effizient am Energiemarkt optimiert.
Bist Du bereit für Lösungen, die mehr als nur ein Versprechen sind und täglich echte Lebensqualität in tausende Haushalte bringen? Was du bei Enpal gestaltest, liefert morgen sauberen Strom und verändert nachhaltig, wie wir Energie nutzen.
Deine Aufgaben
Du optimierst und standardisierst Ops-Prozesse entlang der Supply Chain mit Fokus auf Logistik, Materialplanung, Einkauf und Warehousing .
Du identifizierst Ineffizienzen , führst Root-Cause-Analysen durch und setzt messbare Verbesserungen um (z. B. Lead Times, Bestände, Lieferperformance, Fehlteile).
Du baust Analysen, Dashboards und Reporting für die operative Steuerung (E2E-Transparenz, Bottlenecks, SLA- und Ticket-Tracking).
Du definierst und steuerst zentrale KPIs (z. B. OTIF, Inventory Accuracy, Stock Turns, Backlog, Ticket Aging) inkl. Interpretation und Maßnahmenableitung.
Du treibst End-to-End Projekte : Scope/Business Case, Priorisierung, Umsetzung, Rollout, Adoption und nachhaltige Verankerung (SOPs, Trainings).
Du managst Stakeholder cross-funktional in Operations sowie an den Schnittstellen zu Product (u. a. Leads Product) und Tech (Daten, Automatisierung, Tooling).
Du lieferst klare Recommendations und Updates im direkten Reporting an die Managing Directors (Reviews, Entscheidungen, Maßnahmen-Tracking).
Dein Profil
2 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung in Operations / Supply Chain , Prozessoptimierung, Analytics oder einem vergleichbaren, datengetriebenen Umfeld.
Background aus High-Performance-Umfeldern (Start-up/Scale-up, Unternehmensberatung , PE/VC , Venture Building) ist starkes Plus.
Du kombinierst Analytical Excellence mit Ownership : du arbeitest strukturiert, entscheidungsorientiert und bringst Themen konsequent ins Ziel.
Du bist stark im Stakeholdermanagement (Alignment, Entscheidungsfindung, Konfliktlösung, klare Kommunikation).
Du hast Erfahrung in KPI-Setup und Reporting/Dashboards (z. B. Data aggregation in Snowflake/AirTable + Data visualization in Tableau/PowerBI).
Du kannst Anforderungen sauber zwischen Ops, Product und Tech übersetzen.
Deutsch und Englisch fließend.
Du bist interessiert, auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen erfüllst? Bewirb dich trotzdem! Wir freuen uns darauf, dein Potenzial zu entdecken - unabhängig davon, ob deine Erfahrung jede einzelne Voraussetzung erfüllt. ☀️

In this role, you will be the absolute engine of cross-divisional execution. You will collaborate daily with Product, Growth, Tech, Marketing, and Data teams to push critical business programs across the finish line.

The entrepreneurial “get things done fast” is the most important criteria for Sunday. Own the Program & Project Lifecycle: Take immediate charge of tracking active cross-divisional programs, ensuring milestones are achieved on time and operational friction or project leakage is completely neutralized.

Optimize Operational Handoffs: Standardize communication and workflows at critical project handoff points by ensuring all teams adhere strictly to formalized entry and exit criteria.

The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:
Mews is looking for an Operations Manager to own first-line operational excellence across our Fintech environment. This is a hands-on accountability role for someone who wants to own outcomes in the detail: third-party operations, new-product readiness, customer support and complaints, operational risk, and service performance.
You will report directly to the CEO and operate as a senior first-line owner with visibility across leadership, the Board, and relevant stakeholders. Success in this role means orchestrating delivery, maintaining control, driving performance, and ensuring the service runs smoothly for customers.

This role partners closely with our Operations Resilience Manager (ORM). The Operations Manager keeps the service running and the customer experience on track. The ORM focuses on resilience, recoverability, and control effectiveness.
What you would do
Own third-party operations end to end, acting as the main point of contact for vendors and holding providers to account on onboarding, due diligence, performance, compliance, and issue resolution.
Lead operational readiness for new products and material changes, coordinating review, follow-up, and impact assessment to ensure changes land smoothly and are fully supportable.
Act as the key operational link between different stakeholder groups ensuring strong coordination across support, incident response, and third-party delivery.
Oversee customer support and complaints, ensuring issues are resolved promptly, fairly, and in line with internal standards and other expectations.
Own operational risk and SLA monitoring, using clear indicators and reporting to keep senior management and the Board informed and to escalate risks early.
Support continuity during incidents and disruption scenarios, managing customer and operational impact while partnering closely with the ORM on the wider incident and resilience framework.
Keep operational records accurate and audit-ready, and support internal, external, and other reviews across third-party management and operational controls.
What you would bring
5+ years of experience in operations within payments, fintech, financial services, or a similarly controlled environment.
Genuine hands-on delivery experience, not purely oversight from a distance.
Strong experience across third-party governance, regulatory compliance, and customer operations.
Exposure to operational resilience and business continuity is a strong plus.
Strong project management, communication, and relationship-building skills.
Comfortable owning end-to-end operational processes in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment.
High attention to detail, strong judgement, and a high bar for accuracy and accountability.
Credibility to operate as a first-line owner with senior leadership, Board, and regulator visibility.

The Finance Operations Manager is responsible for overseeing payroll operations, banking and cash activities, VAT compliance coordination, and wider operational finance controls across the Group.
The role acts as the central coordination point between internal stakeholders and outsourced providers across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring the accurate, timely, and compliant delivery of payroll, payments, VAT, and regulatory processes.
This position combines strong operational finance capability with experience managing outsourced providers, international finance operations, and financial controls within a multi-entity environment.
The role focuses on the coordination, review, control, and operational oversight of outsourced and internally managed finance operations processes, rather than acting as the technical specialist responsible for preparing all underlying submissions directly.
The role currently has line management responsibility for the junior finance team members supporting accounts payable, payment processing, and VAT administration activities.
The finance function is also undergoing ongoing systems and process improvement initiatives to further strengthen operational efficiency, controls, and automation across the Group.

Technical Knowledge & Process Depth
The successful candidate will demonstrate a deep understanding of operational finance processes and the principles that underpin them. We are looking for someone who can clearly explain how processes work, why they exist, and how they connect to wider business objectives. The ability to break down complex processes, communicate them effectively to others, and support process improvement will be essential. In Practice you will be:
Able to build a P11D process from first principles
Able to articulate the end-to-end logic of a payroll run, identify where errors typically arise, and explain reconciliation steps to a junior colleague
Understands the VAT return process well enough to review submissions critically, not just pass information to advisors
Can walk through a payment run control framework and identify the risk points
Knows what KYC and international compliance documentation looks like and why it matters — not just where to file it
Essential Experience
Part-qualified or qualified (ACCA, CIMA, ACA or equivalent) with a strong operational finance background
Strong practical experience in payroll coordination, treasury management, and finance operations within a complex organisational structure.
Strong, demonstrable understanding of UK payroll processes and employment tax — including P11D, benefits-in-kind, pensions, and statutory payments
Proven experience working with outsourced payroll providers — managing the review and sign-off of their work
Practical experience overseeing banking platforms, payment controls, mandates and signatories
Direct experience coordinating VAT and compliance processes across multiple jurisdictions
Experience supervising or reviewing junior team members' work and communicating process logic clearly
Confident communicating with senior stakeholders, external providers, and international teams — written and verbal
Desirable
Experience within architecture, professional services, consultancy, or international project-based businesses
Exposure to international payroll operations and overseas banking — particularly China operations
Experience supporting finance systems improvements or automation initiatives
Familiarity with Sage 200, Deltek, or equivalent ERP/project systems
Language skills an advantage
Personal Attributes
We are a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and this role carries significant responsibility over sensitive financial data and processes. We are looking for someone who:
Is genuinely humble, willing to ask questions, acknowledge gaps, and learn the business
Is highly intelligent and intellectually curious — able to pick up new processes quickly and understand them deeply, not just operationally
Communicates with clarity and patience — able to explain complex processes simply to colleagues at all levels, including junior team members and non-finance stakeholders
Takes ownership without being asked — reliable, organised, and delivery-focused
Is calm, approachable and collaborative
Can be trusted with sensitive payroll, banking and compliance information — discretion is essential

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life.

More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between.

Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'.

The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at .
The Opportunity 🚀
This role serves as the operational backbone of the Global Clinical Operations (GCO) team, developing a deep understanding of GCO's day-to-day workings in order to help operationalize its running.

You'll coordinate new projects, identify the right stakeholders, and partner closely with the GCO team, including GCO clinical leadership, to keep programs running smoothly. This is a hands-on operations role where success is measured by reliable execution, clean reporting, and strong cross-functional coordination.

You'll be the connective tissue between GCO sub-teams and partners across product, commercial, GTM, and customer success, giving you visibility into how clinical operations decisions ripple across the business.
What You’ll Own 💼

Serve as the operations point person across GCO sub-teams, keeping frameworks, timelines, and ways of working consistent.
Coordinate the GCO components of new projects end-to-end: identify stakeholders, track deliverables, and keep work moving across global clinical operations, product, and other partner teams.
Track spend against program budgets, flagging variances to leadership.
Spot and help close gaps or silos between GCO sub-teams by maintaining regular alignment touchpoints.
Build and maintain dashboards and reporting infrastructure that give leadership real-time visibility into program status, trends, and open decisions.
Pull together monthly operational updates, synthesizing data from Jira, Zendesk, Airtable, Salesforce, BI tools, and other program analytics into clear, actionable summaries.
Help connect operational metrics to clinical and business outcomes so leadership has a clear line of sight from day-to-day activity to impact.
Serve as a connector between GCO and commercial, GTM, and customer success teams, ensuring the right subject-matter expert is looped into RFPs, RFIs, and retention/expansion conversations.
Ensure feedback from client-facing teams is incorporated into GCO program planning and prioritization.
Identify opportunities to use AI tools, automation, and workflow improvements to save the team time and reduce manual work.
Support team members in getting up to speed on new tools and best practices as they're introduced.

What Success Looks Like 📈
In your first 12–18 months, you will have: Created and rolled out dashboards and reporting infrastructure that are adopted by GCO leadership.Improved operational efficiency across GCO, including reduced redundant meetings and streamlined recurring processes.Established a strong working rhythm with key GCO leadership and cross-functional partners.

Successfully managed multiple projects concurrently, hitting key milestones and deadlines, with consistent reporting/status updates so stakeholders always know where each project stands.

A Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, public health, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience in clinical/healthcare operations.
Demonstrated, hands-on experience in scheduling, budgets, and cross-functional coordination within clinical operations.
Strong program and process-design skills, shown through a program management certification or 2+ years of project management experience, including building/maintaining SOPs, governance documentation, and decision-informing reporting.
High comfort level with modern productivity and data tools (Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, Salesforce, Airtable, BI dashboards) and the ability to quickly learn new systems, including AI-enabled tools.
A demonstrated ability to operate across multiple fast-moving workstreams simultaneously without losing track of details.
Strong documentation skills, with the ability to create and maintain clear, reusable, well-organized documentation.
Extreme organization, with the ability to manage and maintain large databases and datasets accurately.
The ability to establish a process and cadence for audits, ensuring data and documentation stay accurate and current over time.

Experience in reproductive and/or hormonal health (fertility, pregnancy, menopause, low testosterone, gender-affirming care) and related coverage/benefit policies.
A track record of using data to drive decisions — defining KPIs, building dashboards, running monthly/quarterly operational reviews.
Comfortable operating in high-growth, ambiguous environments with a bias toward scalable systems and automation.

Why This Role Matters 🧡
This role sits at the center of Carrot's Global Clinical Operations function, translating day-to-day execution into the reporting and coordination that leadership relies on to make decisions.

By keeping GCO's sub-teams aligned and connecting clinical operations to commercial and customer-facing teams, this person directly shapes how reliably Carrot delivers on its clinical programs — and how clearly that impact gets communicated across the business.

Why Candidates Join Carrot 🌍 Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission. Highlights include:
A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.

At Instructure , we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:
Foundry is a new division inside Instructure, built to generate new revenue with AI-built products. We operate as a portfolio of small pods, each charged with one product bet, under tight weekly governance. They operate independently, with dedicated resources, separate from the core business on purpose: different pace, different governance, and different rewards.
Our goal is to generate meaningful revenue within 12 to 18 months, so this isn’t an innovation lab. We’re building scaled businesses that customers pay for and retain well, and we’re measuring ourselves on revenue, not activity.
Instructure reaches roughly half of higher education in the United States, connecting a credential network of more than 13,000 institutions. Pair that distribution and data with a fast-moving team that builds leanly, and you have something no competitor has. That’s the opportunity New Markets exists to take.
How we work
A pod is two people: a Founder and a Builder, both hands on, close to the customer. The bet is deliberate: we invest in agent-developer tooling and tokens, not in headcount. An operating team of growth marketing, revenue operations, sales overlay, and G&A supports every pod, so founders stay on building products.
Every pod inherits an underlying platform with common design, development, and deployment harnesses, so no pod rebuilds the plumbing. Each pod runs through key phases with regular checkpoints where a governing board reviews progress or recommends a pivot or kill.
The rhythm is fast and transparent. Investor-style updates go out weekly. Demos and keep-or-kill checkpoints happen twice a month. Transparency is the operating model.

You’re the operational engine behind New Markets’ newest product bets. You’ll own the end-to-end go-to-market lifecycle for pod products, from market sizing and early strategy through launch, performance tracking, and the handoff when a product graduates into the core.

When a pod proves customers will pay, you make that motion repeatable and hand it to the full seller base. This is a blank-page job: the playbook doesn’t exist yet, and you’ll write it. The role reports directly to the President, New Markets, with a matrixed dotted line to Instructure’s Go-to-Market Strategy and Operations leadership.
What you’ll own
You own go-to-market operations across the portfolio, and you’re the voice of the New Markets business in the rooms where commercial decisions get made.

Own the end-to-end GTM lifecycle for pod products. Carry each product from market sizing and early strategy through launch planning, field execution, and post-launch performance tracking.
Shape the go-to-market approach with each pod. Partner with Pod Founders, marketing, and the sales overlay on ideal-customer definition, pricing and packaging input, channel strategy, and competitive positioning.
Design the sales motion. Build the coverage models, pipeline processes, forecasting cadences, and rules of engagement for the first seller cohort on each product.
Build the reporting backbone. Stand up and maintain the analytics in Salesforce and Excel that track pipeline health, win/loss, attach rates, average contract value, and renewal trends, and turn that data into insight leadership can act on.
Run launch readiness. Lead CRM buildout in Salesforce, playbook documentation, tool configuration, and alignment across enablement, marketing, finance, deal desk, and IT.
Own the graduation playbook. Define the criteria and the integration motion for products that complete a pod’s journey, so the full seller base can carry and sell the product without a messy handoff.
Be the voice of the business. Translate early-stage complexity into clear, data-backed narratives in planning forums, business reviews, and executive sessions, and support annual planning across capacity, quota, incentive design, and growth roadmaps.
What we expect
Blank page to operating framework. You go from nothing to a working system without a lot of hand-holding, then improve it as results and field feedback come in.
Rigor under ambiguity. You structure messy, early-stage go-to-market problems, build the analytical frame, and land a recommendation you can defend.
Accuracy you stand behind. The insights and reporting you put in front of leadership are right, and you own them.
Influence without authority. You move product, finance, marketing, and sales toward a shared plan without managing any of them.

Five or more years in sales operations, revenue operations, or a related go-to-market function.
Real experience supporting new-product launches or emerging-business initiatives, where the playbook didn’t exist yet.
Three or more years hands-on in Salesforce, building and maintaining reports, dashboards, and data structures.
Advanced Excel, comfortable building models, running variance analysis, and turning raw data into decision-ready output.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentations. A bachelor’s degree is preferred.
Your first 90 days
Month 1. Immerse yourself in the New Markets portfolio, the key stakeholders, and the current go-to-market infrastructure. Understand where each product sits in its lifecycle and find the most pressing operational gaps.
Month 3. Establish a clear view of performance across active pods: pipeline health, coverage, and leading indicators. Build or refine the reporting framework in Salesforce and Excel, and set a recurring operating rhythm with product and sales leadership.
Month 6. Own and drive the go-to-market motion for at least one pod through a checkpoint. Deliver an integration-readiness recommendation for any product approaching graduation, and present a prioritized roadmap for improving New Markets go-to-market operations to senior leadership.

We’re looking for a senior operator to own the quality bar behind Harvey’s human evaluations. As we scale globally, the volume of eval work is growing 10x, but volume only matters if the output is trusted. This role makes Human Data’s signal decision-grade: rigorous, calibrated, and reproducible enough that Product, Engineering, and AI Research act on it to ship.
As a member of our Evaluation Operations team, you’ll work alongside our Evaluation Operations Manager (who runs throughput and coordination) and partner closely with Applied Legal Researchers, Product, Engineering, and AI Research. You'll set the standard for what "good" looks like across eval data and methodology, and certify that results are sound before teams rely on them, building the stakeholder trust that lets EPD act on the signal.

Own the quality bar for Harvey’s human evaluations: define what “good” looks like for eval data and make outputs decision-grade for EPD
Author and maintain the evaluation guidelines, instructions, benchmarks, and gold references that contract attorneys work from, and serve as the arbiter on ambiguous or disputed judgments
Standardize and streamline rubric and evaluation design into repeatable templates and one documented methodology, partnering with Applied Legal Research (ALR), who supplies feature-specific legal depth
Own contract-attorney quality: onboarding, calibration training, inter-rater reliability, and the feedback loop that keeps judgment consistent across attorneys and over time
Define and maintain the failure-mode / error taxonomy that turns raw eval results into a structured, prioritized signal Product and ALR can act on
Run QA on vendor and contract-attorney deliverables against a defined bar before results inform a launch decision
Ensure the quality bar holds across jurisdictions and non-English geographies as coverage expands
Establish one standard, documented way to analyze eval results, and build lightweight operational dashboards to track rater capability and eval-program health
Support ALR in a review step that certifies an evaluation is sound before it scales to contract attorneys
Partner with ALR and Analytics to determine where human eval aligns with online signal and where it can provide expanded insights
What You Have

The Partner Enablement Operations Manager is a senior operator and builder responsible for designing and running a scalable, predictable, and data-driven operating model for partner enablement at Databricks.
This role serves as the operational backbone and strategic integrator for partner enablement, connecting global strategy to the execution across AMER, EMEA, and APJ regions while ensuring programs are delivered consistently, efficiently, and at scale.
The ideal candidate brings strong executive presence, systems thinking, and a bias for automation. They know how to reduce operational friction, build governance that scales, and introduce AI-enabled workflows that improve responsiveness without adding unnecessary complexity or headcount.
We are looking for a builder who can architect operating systems and drive scalability and excellence for the future.

Own the partner enablement operating model, including core planning cadences, governance mechanisms, and execution frameworks that connect strategy to execution.
Run QBRs, MBRs, and executive reviews for partner enablement leadership, using clear metrics and forward-looking insights to drive accountability and decision-making.
Lead end-to-end execution of partner enablement initiatives, ensuring timelines, dependencies, and deliverables are managed effectively across functions and regions.
Build and maintain dashboards and operating reviews that surface partner engagement, program performance, risk signals, and areas requiring intervention.
Act as a key point of contact for cross-regional operational issues and escalations, resolving immediate friction while converting recurring issues into structural improvements.
Design and implement scalable workflows, SOPs, SLAs, and intake mechanisms that improve consistency, reduce manual effort, and create a better experience for internal stakeholders and partners.
Introduce AI-enabled and automation-first workflows for intake, reporting, support, certification, and partner operations where they can safely improve speed, quality, and scale.
Collaborate closely with the Partner organization, Learning and Enablement, Professional Services, and other cross-functional teams to remove friction and improve execution across the partner ecosystem.
Partner closely with the broader operations business to drive cross-functional leverage of ideas and excellence, ensuring new methods and operational innovations are scaled beyond just partner operations.
Establish clear ownership models, decision rights, and governance guardrails to support regional nuance without creating shadow processes or operational inconsistencies.

10+ years of experience in Learning Operations, Program Management, Professional Services Operations, or a related operational leadership field in a high-growth technology environment.
Proven experience supporting global or multi-region teams and translating central strategy into executable operating plans.
Preferred experience in the Data & AI space, with a strong understanding of Databricks' platform capabilities, key differentiators, and end-to-end solutions, and the ability to work effectively with technical stakeholders.
Demonstrated ownership of operating cadence, forecasting, planning, and execution frameworks in a complex, matrixed environment.
Strong analytical capability and the ability to turn data into executive insight, operational decisions, and measurable business outcomes.
Experience improving processes and workflows, with a clear track record of reducing manual effort and increasing scale through automation or AI-enabled solutions.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions without direct authority.
Ability to work independently, manage priorities across time zones, and drive execution in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
Must be open to working a flexible schedule, including frequent late hours to accommodate discussions with the broader enablement team and partner liaisons, the majority of whom are based in the AMER timezone.

Experience in partner enablement, customer education, learning operations, or training operations.
Deep expertise working with and for System Integrators (SIs) and ISVs, with a strong grasp of their core operational principles and business models.
Fluency with AI tools, workflow automation, and analytics platforms used to streamline operations and generate actionable insights.
Strong commercial and operational acumen, including comfort with utilization, forecasting, partner spend, margin thinking, or RevOps-aligned execution.
Experience operating in a highly matrixed international environment with sensitivity to regional and cultural nuance.

You will play a central role in shaping how partner enablement scales at Databricks.
This is a high-visibility role with meaningful impact, offering the opportunity to build a more efficient, governed, and AI-enabled operating model that helps our partner ecosystem grow with the business.
If you enjoy turning ambiguity into structure, building systems that remove friction, and helping teams scale through better operations rather than more manual work, this role is for you.
Success Metrics
Operational Predictability: Build a disciplined partner enablement operating cadence where risks are surfaced early and execution is measurable and consistent.
Stakeholder Experience and Self-Sufficiency: Increase the percentage of standard partner enablement requests handled through structured, low-touch, or self-service workflows.
Escalation Management and Process Resilience: Reduce recurring operational friction by improving escalation handling, clarifying ownership, and improving systemic resolution of recurring issues.
Scalable Execution: Improve throughput, consistency, and delivery quality across global partner enablement programs without relying on incremental manual work.
AI-Enabled Transformation: Deploy practical AI-enabled workflows that improve speed, visibility, and efficiency across intake, reporting, support, and partner operations.
About Databricks
Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents.

Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn , X , YouTube , and Instagram .

At Databricks, we strive to provide comprehensive benefits and perks that meet the needs of all of our employees. For specific details on the benefits offered in your region click here .
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
At Databricks, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can excel. We take great care to ensure that our hiring practices are inclusive and meet equal employment opportunity standards.

Individuals looking for employment at Databricks are considered without regard to age, color, disability, ethnicity, family or marital status, gender identity or expression, language, national origin, physical and mental ability, political affiliation, race, religion, sexual orientation, socio-economic status, veteran status, and other protected characteristics.

Based in Auckland and reporting to the ANZ CEO, the General Manager for New Zealand leads the overall performance, growth and strategic direction of HelloFresh New Zealand; one of the HelloFresh’s most established and innovative markets.

Owning the New Zealand P&L end-to-end, you set the strategy to maximize sustainable growth and profitability, sharpen the local proposition, and represent HelloFresh with government, regulators, partners and the wider community.

You deliver through influence, aligning matrixed teams across growth, product, marketing, finance, customer care and operations behind a shared plan.
Above all, you will change the way Kiwis eat, forever!

Own the P&L: Take full accountability for HelloFresh New Zealand’s commercial and financial performance, leading annual planning, forecasting and business reviews with ANZ and Global leadership.
Set the strategy: Define and execute the roadmap that returns the market to sustainable growth and profitability across customer acquisition, retention, pricing and margin.
Sharpen the proposition: Partner with Global teams to pilot new products and propositions, and strengthen the local relevance of HelloFresh for Kiwi customers.
Lead through influence: Align and energise matrixed teams across growth, product, marketing, finance, customer care and operations to reach shared business objectives without direct line authority.
Represent the business: Act as the senior spokesperson for HelloFresh New Zealand with government, regulators, industry bodies and strategic partners.
Shape Group strategy: Feed insight, innovation and learnings from New Zealand back into regional and Global decision-making.

P&L leadership: A track record of owning a P&L or a major commercial function, ideally blending top-tier consulting, high-growth startup or comparable fast-paced experience.
Commercial and product instinct: Strong grounding in D2C marketing and product development, with the judgement to turn strategy into measurable growth.
Influence without authority: The ability to set clear direction and bring senior, matrixed stakeholders along through collaboration rather than formal reporting lines.
Data-driven mindset: A highly analytical approach, comfortable using data to prioritise and to hold the business to its plan.
Local market understanding: Familiarity with the New Zealand market and consumer, or a real ability to build local relevance and credibility quickly.
Drive and food enthusiasm: Entrepreneurial energy, resilience and a genuine enthusiasm for good food and the HelloFresh mission.

Compensation with upside: A highly attractive package with significant equity upside for a senior leader in a leading global food-technology company.
Own a market: The rare chance to lead an entire market and shape its direction end to end.
Hybrid working: Three days in the Auckland office and two days working from home each week.
Work from anywhere: Up to three weeks working from a location of your choice in any 12-month period.
Wellbeing support: Free Headspace access (extendable to five friends or family) and a confidential Employee Assistance Program.
Learning and growth: HelloFresh Academy sessions, a function-led L&D budget and a structured mentoring program.
Time to recharge: Additional HF Days that grow with tenure, plus sabbatical leave for longer-serving team members.
HelloFresh discount: 70% off your HelloFresh boxes, plus friends-and-family discounts.
Are you the missing ingredient? If this sounds like a tasty opportunity, we’d be excited to hear from you. We aim to review your profile and respond within 5 business days.

We're transforming the grocery industry
At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community.

We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.
Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.
Instacart is a Flex First team
There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Why this role is on the menu
Eversight, part of Instacart, is building next-generation data insights and analytics platforms that help leading CPGs & Retailers make smarter, faster decisions across pricing, promotions, retail media, and omni-commerce.

We're hiring a Senior Revenue Operations Manager to build and run end-to-end revenue operations across our Commercial organization (Sales and Customer Success), spanning both CPG and Retail.

This is a build-and-own role, not a request-response one: you'll identify what the business needs before it's escalated to you, bring a recommendation, and drive it to completion.

You'll report directly to the Director of Sales Capabilities & Strategy, with broad latitude to design process, own reporting, and act as a trusted partner to commercial leadership across Eversight Sales, Customer Success, and Product, along with cross functional partners like Strategic Finance, Commercial Partnerships and Brand Partnerships.
What you'll cook up in your first year
Standardized reporting and forecasting models live across CPG and Retail, giving commercial leadership one clear view of pipeline, renewals, and customer health
Dashboards built and adopted across Sales and Customer Success that leadership actually uses to make decisions, tracking pipeline, renewal rate, expansion, and churn risk
Operational gaps identified and fixed before anyone had to ask, each tied to a measurable improvement in forecast accuracy, data integrity, or process efficiency
AI tools, agents, and workflow automations built and shipped that eliminate recurring reporting and data cleanup work, cutting manual operational overhead across the commercial org
Trusted operational relationships built across every team you touch, with clean handoffs and no surprises
Process documentation and standardized frameworks built as you go, not bolted on after the fact

Bachelor's degree in Business, Analytics, Statistics, or related field
7+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or a similar function within a SaaS company; experience in CPG, Retail, or trade promotion/pricing analytics highly preferred
Proven ability to analyze and interpret complex data sets to deliver actionable insight
Fluent in using AI tools, agents, and workflow automations to eliminate manual reporting and data cleanup, as a core part of how you operate rather than an occasional add-on
Experience with SQL and Tableau
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present findings to leadership
Demonstrated ability to identify challenges, prioritize solutions, and execute improvements independently
Adept at working cross-functionally with a focus on aligning multiple stakeholders toward shared goals
A self-starter able to operate independently in a fast-paced environment

MBA
Working knowledge of Salesforce and Planhat (or comparable CS platform)
Understanding of the CPG trade promotion, pricing, and revenue growth management landscape
Understanding of the Retail Merchandising landscape

Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family.

The base pay for this role is: $106,812.00 - $140,190.75 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program and annual performance bonuses.

Manage Oscar’s Content Management System (CMS) and ensure it is optimized for internal use, including content updates, landing page creation, and form functionality.

Train internal teams (e.g., Compliance, Pharmacy) on best practices and self-service content updates.
Ensure accurate set up of Google Analytics to monitor website performance, user behavior, and key metrics, reporting insights and opportunities to stakeholders.
Drive and manage A/B testing strategies and collaborate with internal teams to identify and implement optimization opportunities.
Ensure the company’s digital presence is protected and aligned with business goals.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align website goals with broader business objectives.

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.
At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.
A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
Our Recruiting Team plays a vital role in shaping exceptional teams at Roblox and driving our future growth.

At the center of the recruiting experience is our Recruiting Coordination team, who handle everything from scheduling interviews, tracking candidate data and helping improve internal processes all while ensuring a positive experience for all candidates.

We are looking for a motivated Recruiting Coordinator to join our team and contribute to the next stage of Roblox's success! This position is a twelve-month short-term employment with the opportunity to be considered for extension and/or full-time employment pending performance and business needs.

This is a hybrid position based in our San Mateo, CA offices.
You Will
Partner with members of our recruiting and hiring teams to create a phenomenal candidate experience
Manage the candidate interview process including scheduling a high-volume of interviews and being the contact for day-of questions
Greeting, hosting, and managing the experience for candidates visiting the office for in-person interviews
Oversee and facilitate a seamless candidate onsite experience, ensuring a positive welcome for all visitors.
Manage high-complexity operational workflows, including job approvals, Talent Review coordination, offer letter generation, and interview scheduling, ensuring data accuracy and compliance while maintaining exceptional stakeholder relationships and a white-glove candidate experience.
Maintain adherence to established SLAs and actively monitor time-to-schedule, time-to-approve and ticket resolution metrics, ensuring high velocity and operational integrity.
Proactively own and solve the root cause of scheduling and operational challenges or inconsistencies

2+ years of experience with a proven history of managing high-volume, complex operational tasks. Experience with Greenhouse and the recruiting space is preferred.
Exceptional Attention to Detail: Proven ability to reliably manage operational tasks with accuracy in high-stakes, complex and in some cases, confidential environments
Strong Stakeholder Partnership & Communication: Demonstrated ability to frame communication around stakeholder needs, influence outcomes, and communicate with impact and empathy.
A Strategic Mindset: Demonstrated systems thinking and experience designing processes/guardrails to solve problems at scale.
High-Volume/High-Velocity Execution: Ability to manage a high volume of requests, prioritize rapid response times, and handle scheduling requests with precision and speed.

A Curious Problem Solver: Demonstrated ability to perform initial research and diagnosis of issues, consolidating questions and proposing pre-vetted options or solutions back to stakeholders, TA and hiring teams when requests are incomplete or unclear.
Data-Fluent: Able to use and translate data into actionable solutions when partnering with others.
Proactive and Accountable: Own the outcome of your processes and routinely propose pre-vetted options and Plan Bs instead of just reporting a problem.
Timely and Professional Communicator: Ensure all candidate communication is professional, timely, and detail-oriented, reflecting a white-glove candidate experience.
Committed to Service Delivery: View your service as the foundation of trust for candidates and stakeholders, recognizing that dependability is the team's currency.

ICT\-Security Operations Manager\*in
Werde Teil unseres Teams
Deine Arbeit hat Wirkung – für Bern und für die Menschen, die hier leben und arbeiten. Gestalte mit uns die Gemeinschaft und die Zukunft dieser Stadt: sichtbar, spürbar, nachhaltig.
Die Direktion Finanzen, Personal und Informatik erbringt vielfältige stadtinterne Dienstleistungen und stellt zentrale Ressourcen bereit. Bedienen, steuern, weiterentwickeln und überwachen der unternehmensweiten ICT\-Sicherheitssysteme
Beurteilen der Wirksamkeit der getroffenen Sicherheitsvorkehrungen und Initiieren von weiteren Massnahmen zur Verbesserung der Sicherheit
Analysieren von sicherheitsrelevanten Ereignissen und deren möglichen Auswirkungen auf ICT\-Systeme hinsichtlich Hardware, Software, Kommunikationsnetzen und \-diensten
Einleiten und Koordinieren von Sofortmassnahmen wie z.B. Schutz\-, Übergangs\-, Ausweich\- und Eskalationsmassnahmen im Falle sicherheitsbedrohender Ereignisse
Mitarbeiten beim Evaluieren und Beschaffen von Sicherheitssystemen und \-tools
Was du mitbringst
Abgeschlossene Berufslehre im Informatik\-Umfeld und weiterführende Ausbildungen wie z.B. HF, FH (idealerweise im Cyber Security\-Bereich)
Praxiserfahrung im Bereich der operativen IT\-Sicherheit (Loganalyse, SIEM, Schwachstellenmanagement), insbesondere auch im Microsoft\-Umfeld (MS Defender)
Kommunikative und teamfähige Persönlichkeit
Hohes Mass an Selbstständigkeit, persönlichem Engagement und Flexibilität
Kontaktfreudigkeit und die Bereitschaft, sich rasch in neue Arbeitsgebiete einzuarbeiten
Gute Deutsch\- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

Dein Bewerbungsprozess

s.h: So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess bei uns ab
s.t:
Schritt 1: Online Bewerbung
Reiche deine Bewerbungsunterlagen online über unser Jobportal ein. Damit wir deine Unterlagen weiterbearbeiten können, musst du ein Login erstellen. Nachdem du deine Bewerbung eingereicht hast, erhältst du eine Bestätigung. Wir beurteilen jede Bewerbung individuell anhand der Kriterien im Stelleninserat. Das braucht manchmal etwas Zeit. Wenn deine Bewerbung passt, kontaktieren wir dich für ein erstes Gespräch.

## Where passion meets opportunity ##
The best of your adventures is the one you have yet to sail!
## Your Purpose ##
We are pleased to be hiring for an Environmental Operations Manager to join our growing Enviromental department. In this role you will manage all operational environmental activities of MSC Cruises fleet of cruise vessels ensuring operational excellence and adherence to all applicable environmental rules and regulations and Company Policy.

* Plans and manages logistics and waste disposal activities, ensuring the full compliance with all applicable regulations and Company policies;
* Monitors vessels- activities daily in order to ensure their compliance with all applicable environmental regulations and company policies. Drives operational fleet activities through daily communication with the ship commands and onboard officers;
* Participates in audit inspections, and ISO 14001 and 21070 certifications as required.
* Manages the administrative and operational environmental activities with Port Agencies and stakeholders, developing strategies and programs;
* Analyses budget and disbursement accounts for managed vessels and provides input to Head of Fleet Environmental Operations.
* Coordinates shipside activities, ensuring appropriate documentation, related to CLIA, Port Authorities and other stakeholders;
* Deals with environmental services vendors and Agencies in order to ensure the ships- environmental compliance, negotiating costs/rebates and provides support for any relevant financial matters;
* Reviews and ensures the correct application of procedures, Manuals, Record Books, and all applicable environmental related documentation;
* Researches, follows and updates environmental legislation, and national and international rules regarding all environmental matters;
* Administers all reporting schemes (ESI, EPI, MRV, IMO DCS, Ocean Guardian etc) for managed vessels and reports results to Head of Fleet Environmental Operations.
* Analyses new business opportunities in order to optimize the full waste management and water supply process for the fleet, including the new building projects. Analyses costs and environmental performances and cooperates with Port Operations in the development of programs in the environmental related area;
* Cooperates in all Environmental Department projects and with all multidisciplinary projects involving different MSC Cruises Departments.
* Participates and assist with the fleet training program and managed vessels as required by the Head of Environmental Systems Training & Audit.
* Assists with the administration of the overall environmental program at Ocean Cay, including but not limited to waste management, training, compliance, audit, and reporting.
* Performs other relevant tasks as required by operational departmental needs.
## Your Journey so far ##
· Fluent in oral and written English. Knowledge of Italian and other major European languages is an advantage.
· Environmental science university studies preferred. Post-graduate specific studies in the area of interest preferred.
· A wide knowledge of the Cruise/Maritime industry (preferred).
· Experience onboard cruise ships as either Environmental Officer for a minimum of three years (preferred), or
Deck Officer / Engineer Officer with at least two years of professional experience in ashore environmental
related roles.
· Some of the above requirements can also be fulfilled by having three years plus of working experience in
environmental-related sector.
· Ability to use Microsoft Office and other company specific operating platforms and databases.
· Able to manage communication at all levels. Proven ability to lead and contribute to a harmonious and
productive team environment.
· Ability to understand and interpret various complex regulations and environmental matters.
· Ability to understand and interpret various financial matters affecting the Department.
· Ability to work in a multicultural and international working environment.
· Ability to perform under pressure.
## Your Essentials ##
* Fluent in oral and written English. Knowledge of Italian and other major European languages is an advantage;
* The existing right to live and work in the EU is required
## Our commitment ##
We are committed to building a future that values diverse perspectives, embraces the world beyond borders, and fosters an inclusive environment where every individual feels valued, respected and empowered to be their authentic selves. Our commitment extends to taking meaningful, measurable actions that have a long-term positive impact on our guests, our employees and our planet.
Ready to turn your passion into something extraordinary? Join us at MSC Cruises, where new opportunities await. Apply today to be part of a global team that is pushing boundaries and achieving something remarkable. Your journey starts here!
